newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi says budget can be altered but not distorted.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says budget can be altered but not distorted.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that his controversial 1997 budget can be altered but not distorted.
Prodi, talking to reporters ahead of a Italian-French summit in Naples, said the government was not opposed to parliament debating individual sections of the budget.
But he said the entire budget could not be "distorted."
"The parameters of reference cannot be changed," he said.
Opposition parties have denouned the cost-cutting budget as being "all-taxes" and even some parties in Prodi's coalition have criticised increases in home and real estate taxes.
The budget, which Prodi says is necessary for Italy to take part in European Monetary Union (EMU), was presented to parliament on Thursday afternoon.
It must be approved by the end of the year.
